verses.restored: Ahab told Jezebel all Elijah had done and all concerning how he killed all the prophets with sword.
Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah, saying, Thus may gods do and thus add, if by this time tomorrow I do not make your life like life of one of them.
He saw/was afraid, arose, and went for his life. He came to Beersheba belonging to Judah and left his servant there.
He went a day's journey into wilderness, came, and sat beneath a broom tree. He asked for his life to die and said, Enough now, YHWH. Take my life, for I am no better than my ancestors.
He lay down and slept beneath one broom tree. Look, a messenger touched him and said, Arise, eat.
He looked, and at his head was a cake baked upon hot stones and a jar of water. He ate, drank, and lay down again.
Messenger of YHWH returned a second time, touched him, and said, Arise, eat, for journey is too much for you.
He arose, ate, and drank, and went in strength of that food forty days and forty nights to Horeb, mountain of Divine.
He came there to a cave and lodged there. Look, word of YHWH came to him and said, What are you doing here, Elijah?

He said, Being zealous, I was zealous for YHWH, Divine of armies, for children of Israel abandoned your covenant, tore down your altars, and killed your prophets with sword. I, I alone, remain, and they seek my life to take it.

YHWH said, Go out and stand upon mountain before YHWH. Look, YHWH passed by: a great and strong wind tore mountains and shattered rocks before YHWH, but YHWH was not in wind; after wind an earthquake, but YHWH was not in earthquake.
After earthquake a fire, but YHWH was not in fire; after fire, a sound of thin silence/a low whisper.
When Elijah heard, he wrapped his face in mantle, went out, and stood at entrance of cave. Look, a voice came to him and said, What are you doing here, Elijah?

He said, Being zealous, I was zealous for YHWH, Divine of armies, for children of Israel abandoned your covenant, tore down your altars, and killed your prophets with sword. I, I alone, remain, and they seek my life to take it.
YHWH said to him, Go, return on your way to wilderness of Damascus. When you come, anoint Hazael as king over Aram.
Jehu son of Nimshi you shall anoint as king over Israel, and Elisha son of Shaphat from Abel-meholah you shall anoint as prophet in your place.
One escaping sword of Hazael Jehu shall kill, and one escaping sword of Jehu Elisha shall kill.
Yet I have left in Israel seven thousand, all knees that did not bow to Baal and every mouth that did not kiss him.
He went from there and found Elisha son of Shaphat plowing, with twelve pairs of cattle before him, and he with twelfth. Elijah passed by him and threw his mantle upon him.
He left cattle, ran after Elijah, and said, Please let me kiss my father and mother, then I will go after you. Elijah said to him, Go, return, for what have I done to you?

He returned from after him, took pair of cattle, sacrificed/slaughtered them, boiled their flesh with equipment of cattle, and gave to people, and they ate. He arose, went after Elijah, and served him.

translation_notes: Elijah's wish to die follows threat, flight, isolation, exhaustion, and the violent aftermath of Carmel. It must be handled as acute suicidal distress, not spiritual drama, cowardice, or a noble desire for death.
The first response is sleep, touch, food, water, and more rest. These are compassionate supports, though modern suicidal crisis also requires immediate human safety planning and professional help.

Elijah says he is alone, but Obadiah preserved one hundred prophets and the chapter later names seven thousand. Trauma and burnout can narrow perception without making the distressed person dishonest.
The Hebrew phrase often rendered 'still small voice' may mean a sound of thin silence. The passage does not teach that the Divine is never present in wind, earthquake, or fire in other texts.
The lethal sequence involving Hazael, Jehu, and Elisha is a disturbing political oracle, not a model for assassination, religious revolution, or claiming Divine authorization to kill opponents.
Jezebel's death threat is accountable violence, but her gender and foreign identity must not become misogynistic or xenophobic shorthand for evil.
Elisha's family farewell is requested rather than forbidden. Calling does not require abrupt severance, coercive control, or abandonment of loved ones.
The cattle are slaughtered and the farming equipment burned for a communal meal. This signals irreversible transition but is not a required ritual for vocation or a license for animal harm.
safety_note: Suicide-safe reading: Elijah's wish to die is met first with rest, food, water, presence, and continued care—not shame. Do not romanticize his despair or imitate lethal commissions. In real danger, seek immediate support and protect life. Calling and spiritual intensity never justify killing, coercion, or severing healthy relationships.
